title: FreshSip Ontario weekend: buy 2, get 1 free

brief.title: FreshSip Ontario weekend campaign
brief.text: Launch a weekend Ontario campaign: buy two eligible FreshSip beverages and receive one free, once per customer, while stock lasts.

clarifications.seeded_rationale: Selected demo decision. Marketing confirmed the offer is meant to bring in new trial, not repeat discounting.
clarifications.gap_note: POL-PROMO §5 requires the brief to state the scope and defines no default.

requirements.title: Buy two eligible units, get one free

criteria.text: With two paid eligible units in the cart, the customer can add exactly one free eligible unit priced at 0.00.
Unrelated products, including FreshSip Sparkling Lime, neither count toward the offer nor can be the free unit.
With fewer than two paid eligible units, no free unit can be added.
Removing qualifying paid units, or making any change that ends eligibility, removes the free unit from the cart and from the total.
The offer applies only when the shipping province is ON. A missing or different province makes the cart ineligible.
The offer is active from 2026-10-31 00:00 to 2026-11-02 00:00 (end exclusive) America/Toronto, converted to UTC as 04:00Z and 05:00Z, which spans the end of DST.
Campaign times that are ambiguous or do not exist in local time (DST transitions) are rejected.
A discount code and the free unit cannot be combined, in either order.

requirements.title: Once per authenticated customer per campaign

criteria.text: Each signed-in customer receives at most one free unit per campaign across all orders. Anonymous carts cannot claim the free unit.
Concurrent checkouts by the same customer redeem at most once.
Stock for paid and free units is reserved when the order is created. Insufficient stock rejects checkout without committing anything.
Cart quotes do not consume a redemption or stock.
A mock payment failure releases the reservation and the redemption.
Repeating a checkout request with the same idempotency key returns the same order, without a second charge or redemption.
A full cancellation refunds the total and restores the entitlement.
A partial return refunds the amount allocated to the unit by the original promotion and does not restore the entitlement.

requirement_sets.source: requirement set v1 + incident INC review (dependency resilience)

adds.title: Fail fast when inventory is unavailable

criteria.text: If the inventory system does not answer within the 2-second budget, checkout returns 'temporarily unavailable' within 3 seconds, keeps the cart, and creates no order.
Checkout succeeds again once the inventory system responds.

design.summary: Add a campaign module to the storefront service. Re-derive the entitlement on every cart recompute. Record the redemption in the same transaction as order creation, using a partial unique index.

components.name: storefront/promotions.py (new)
components.change: Campaign configuration, explicit America/Toronto to UTC conversion, eligibility evaluation, claim and remove free unit, redemption records.

components.name: storefront/pricing.py
components.change: Quotes include free lines and a promotion summary. Discount codes are rejected while a free unit is in the cart.

components.name: storefront/checkout.py
components.change: Promotion-group allocation; pending, then committed or released, redemption inside the order transaction.

components.name: storefront/inventory_adapter.py
components.change: Order-level reservation call that tags campaign units.

rationale: The entitlement is derived state. Recomputing it on every quote avoids stale free lines (REQ-2).
A partial unique index on active redemptions enforces once-per-customer under concurrency (AC-6.2).
Promotion allocation is stored per unit at order time, so refunds never depend on current prices (POL-RET section 2).
